proposal:
# Card 228 mid-card decision: the scope of criterion 1

Raised by the auditor's FLAG: criterion 1 has grown to six red/green cycles (1a to 1f) against a slice that planned one cycle per criterion (D157), with criteria 2 and 3 not started. The facilitator states the options; the team decides.

Facts from git: 1a hidden verbs (05a838f/63e4f61), 1b encoded (82c1e84/fdff54f), 1c non-shell (c743784/9fe3913), 1d git discard, iex and Remove-Item (40555b4/4e35837), 1e interpreters and rsync (025b178/53666c3), 1f hex, wrappers, alias and [char] (red ca59449, green running). Each green ran the full suite (about 30 minutes). What criterion 1's own acceptance (slice lines 44 to 47) still lacks after 1f: the I ZOMBIE (scan_entry, the CLI and facilitator.run_backend give the same findings for one file) and the M ZOMBIE (ten forms in one file give ten lines, duplicates once). The path forms (slice line 65) are a D167 hostile-input list, not a ZOMBIE of criterion 1.

Options:
(a) Finish now: criterion 1 closes after green 1f; the I and M ZOMBIES and the path forms go to a follow-up card.
(b) Cap it: one last cycle, 1g, limited to the I and M ZOMBIES, which are criterion 1's own acceptance; the path forms go to the slice's residual-forms follow-up (F4). After 1g no further criterion-1 cycle on this card; any new form found later is a follow-up card.
(c) Split the remainder: criterion 1 closes after 1f, and a new card takes 1g plus the path forms.

Proposal: option (b). Reason: the I and M ZOMBIES are the acceptance the team adopted for criterion 1, so closing without them leaves criterion 1 unmet, while the path forms are a separate surface the slice already routes to F4. Then criterion 2, then criterion 3. The pre-ship gate counts the cycles per criterion and the retro weighs the increment rule (slice under D157 allowed increments, but no cap was written).

Ask: NO OBJECTION, or OBJECTION with one fixed condition (for example, name option (a) or (c) instead).
